title: Kotlin Features, Advantages, and Limitations
learning_outcomes: Explain the central rule or purpose of kotlin features, advantages, and limitations using at least one correct term from the lesson.
Interpret or adapt a small Kotlin example that demonstrates kotlin features, advantages, and limitations.
Identify one relevant edge case, debugging step, or version/platform constraint.

content.intro: In this lesson, you will learn **Kotlin Features, Advantages, and Limitations** as part of **Introduction to Kotlin**. Apply kotlin features, advantages, and limitations by identifying the required behavior, the relevant Kotlin type/API, and the conditions under which the expected result can fail. Use the subtopics—Static Typing and Type Inference, Null Safety, Concise Syntax and Expressive APIs—as a checklist: predict what the example will do, then verify it in a project configured for the target platform.
content.why_it_matters: Clear fundamentals help you reason about program behavior before adding abstraction. Small input/output checks make syntax and control flow easier to debug.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: Apply kotlin features, advantages, and limitations by identifying the required behavior, the relevant Kotlin type/API, and the conditions under which the expected result can fail.

content_blocks.title: How to reason about it
content_blocks.text: Start with static typing and type inference. Then compare it with null safety. Identify the input, state, dependency, or branch that determines the result. The snippet is a static reference for CodeLeaf and is not executed in the lesson page.

items.title: Static Typing and Type Inference
items.text: Static Typing and Type Inference is one part of kotlin features, advantages, and limitations. Connect its definition to the example, identify the input/state it changes, and verify the expected behavior with a small test case.

items.title: Null Safety
items.text: Null Safety is about representing or handling the possibility that a value is absent. Keep nullability visible in the type and choose an explicit fallback, branch, or result model rather than assuming the value exists.

items.title: Concise Syntax and Expressive APIs
items.text: Concise Syntax and Expressive APIs crosses a system boundary. Model success and failure, validate external data, apply timeout/retry rules deliberately, and keep credentials and database access out of presentation code.

items.title: Interoperability and Ecosystem Trade-offs
items.text: Interoperability and Ecosystem Trade-offs means checking the boundary between the language feature and its compiler, runtime, plugin, library, or target version. Pin the versions used by the project and verify documented support before depending on the behavior.

content_blocks.run_instructions: Save the snippet in a Kotlin/JVM console project and run the configured Gradle application task, or use the Kotlin Playground for examples that need no external dependencies.
content_blocks.reset_steps: Restore the documented starting values, rerun the smallest test, and compare the result with the expected output. If behavior differs, check the compiler/plugin/runtime versions and the active target before changing more than one thing.

content_blocks.title: Common mistake to avoid
content_blocks.text: Kotlin Features, Advantages, and Limitations removes the need to test boundary conditions or verify the chosen runtime/library version.

content_blocks.title: Troubleshooting and reset
content_blocks.text: If the example fails, first confirm which runtime/project type the snippet requires. Read the first useful compiler or runtime message, check imports and declared dependencies, reduce the example to a minimal case, and rerun. For target-specific code, use the target toolchain rather than assuming a console or browser runner can execute it.

items.title: Explain
items.text: Describe the main rule of kotlin features, advantages, and limitations in your own words.

items.title: Apply
items.text: Change one input or condition and predict the result before running it.

items.title: Verify
items.text: Check one edge case and the official reference for the selected Kotlin/runtime version.

content.task: Try it yourself: create a small variation that demonstrates kotlin features, advantages, and limitations. Write down your predicted result first, run it in the correct local project, then explain one boundary case involving static typing and type inference.
task_acceptance_criteria: Explain kotlin features, advantages, and limitations without copying the lesson wording.
Demonstrate the concept with a small code/configuration change and state the expected result.
Test one boundary case or explain a relevant platform/version limitation.
hints: Begin with the first syllabus subtopic: Static Typing and Type Inference. What input or state does it act on?
Change only one value, branch, declaration, or dependency at a time. Predict what should happen before running the code.
Compare your observed result with the expected output and the official reference; verify that you are using the required project type and dependency set.
